papers.version_note: The file is arXiv 2211.07075 version 3 (21 Feb 2024), titled Expressive Quantum Perceptrons for Quantum Neuromorphic Computing; the file name carries the earlier title Universal Quantum Perceptrons. The text layer holds the paper twice (a one-column copy, then a two-column copy of the main text); the two copies are the same text. Page numbers in the stored anchors follow another layout. Figure plots are images; their captions and the surrounding text were read. The second copy was checked word by word against the first and holds no word the first lacks beyond hyphenation fragments.
papers.what_it_is: A theory and simulation paper that defines a quantum perceptron as a star-shaped spin system with one output qubit, argues it recovers classical activation functions and any unitary, and applies it to kernel inner products, entanglement witnessing and time-reversal metrology.

existing.note: The paper's result is conditional: it holds for activation functions with a Fourier series on [-pi, pi], uses fields on the output qubit only, needs a large field amplitude on the output qubit compared with the couplings, and is approximated by a finite number of Fourier terms. The stored value omits these conditions. The word 'prove' appears in the Conclusion; Section II C says 'we show' and points to Appendix A.
existing.value: The authors state that a quantum perceptron with time-dependent single-qubit control fields on the output qubit can generate any bounded and piece-wise continuous activation function that has a Fourier series, and that a series of perceptrons can approximate any multivariable function whose components have a Fourier series; in practice they approximate the gate by a finite number of Fourier terms.
quotes: This calculation illustrates that if we take Eq. (4) with its time-dependent, single-qubit control fields we can generate any bounded and piece-wise continuous activation function.
Thus, a series of perceptrons can approximate any multivariable function as long as the function's components have a Fourier series.
In practice, we approximate the gate UfML by a finite number of Fourier terms
existing.reader_inference: The conclusion uses the verb prove; the body derives the result in an appendix by a Fourier-series construction and checks it numerically only for four activation functions.

Appendix B proves the construction for the Clifford+T gate set, but the input-to-input two-qubit gate is approximate: it comes from second-order perturbation theory in the limit of a large output-qubit field, and the authors give the error as one over that field. existing.value: The authors show that a restricted version of the fields in the quantum perceptron Hamiltonian realizes the Clifford+T universal gate set, so that a quantum perceptron can realize any quantum computation in theory; the gate between two input qubits is approximate, from second-order perturbation theory with a large field on the output qubit.
quotes: To show that a QP can achieve any quantum computation, it suffices to establish that a restricted version of the fields in Eq. (4) achieves a universal gate set.
For concreteness, we show that a QP contains the Clifford+T universal gate set [86].
Since Heff is correct up to order O((fox)−2), the total error is of order O((fox)−1).
This section shows that Eq. (4) can, in theory, cre- ate any quantum computation.
existing.reader_inference: Section II D calls the result 'in practice' in one sentence and 'in theory' in others; the derivation is analytic with no simulation of a universal gate set.

assertions.value: The authors state that universality needs three capabilities: any single-qubit rotation, decoupling qubits that are not wanted, and two-qubit gates between any pair of qubits.
quotes: That is, QPs can do (i) any single-qubit rotation, (ii) decouple qubits in case we do not want to operate on them, and (iii) perform two-qubit gates among any pair of qubits.

assertions.value: The paper derives that a control-Z gate between an input and the output qubit follows from a specific choice of coupling and field values, and that two input qubits interact through the output qubit in second-order perturbation theory.
quotes: Thus, up to an arbitrary phase, a QP plus rotations entangles the input and the output via a CZ gate.
Since inputs i, j interact with the output, they can interact with each other via a second-order interaction.

assertions.value: The authors state that the total error of the input-input control-Z construction is of order one over the output-qubit field, because the effective Hamiltonian is correct to second order in the inverse field.
quotes: Since Heff is correct up to order O((fox)−2), the total error is of order O((fox)−1).

assertions.value: The authors show that rotating an input qubit by a series of pi rotations about the x axis makes the average input-output coupling vanish for an even number of rotations, and state that the second moment of the average Hamiltonian also vanishes.
quotes: Thus, through rotation, we can realize identity gates on average.
all of which vanish. Thus, H2 = 0.

assertions.value: The authors state that the universality proof is given to show a theoretical advantage over classical perceptrons, not to use quantum perceptrons for universal quantum computation like a quantum circuit, and that whether they give practical advantage over classical computation or other quantum paradigms is ongoing research.
quotes: Instead, this proof is presented to show the theoretical advantage of QPs over classical per- ceptrons.

assertions.value: The authors report that the singlet-forming task shows a barren plateau, with the mean gradient flattening to zero and the variance exponentially small in the number of qubits, and they argue it comes from entanglement build-up in the star-like architecture.
quotes: We observe that QPs exhibit barren plateaus where the mean of ∂L flattens out to zero and its variance is exponentially small in the number of qubits.
We argue that this BP results from the large entanglement build-up due to the perceptron's star-like architecture.

assertions.value: The authors define entanglement thinning as a scale-free square-Hoyer regularizer added to the loss, with a strength that is scheduled away during training, and state that it does not raise the sample complexity.
quotes: We call this technique entanglement thinning (ET) which aims to reduce interactions between the input and output qubits.
The square-Hoyer term can be easily calculated in a classical computer and therefore does not increase the sample complexity of a QP.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's definition of its method, Section III A and Eq. (17).

assertions.value: The authors report that with entanglement thinning irrelevant couplings fall below the 10 to the minus 5 threshold, and that over 100 trainings of 200 epochs on a four-qubit perceptron one noncontributing qubit is most often left on at regularization strength 10.

For this plot, we trained 100 times for 200 epochs each on a N = 4 QP.
For r = 10 we find that, most often, only one noncontributing qubit is left on.

quotes: However, for these applications no thinning was necessary.

quotes: However, as shown in Fig. 5(a), QPs do exhibit BPs. This again shows that k-design resemblance is sufficient but not necessary for a VQA to exhibit barren plateaus.

papers.title_in_file: Solvable Quantum Circuits in Tree+1 Dimensions
papers.version_note: The file is arXiv 2503.20927 version 2 (28 Aug 2025), the paper the record names. The text layer holds the paper twice (a one-column copy, then a two-column copy); a word-level comparison found no word in the second copy that the first lacks beyond hyphenation fragments. Many equations and all tensor-network diagrams are images and do not appear in the text layer; the surrounding text and captions were read. Page numbers in the stored anchors follow another layout.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that builds unitary circuits on tree graphs from z-site gates, defines tree-unitarity as a generalization of dual-unitarity, and derives exactly solvable light-cone correlations, out-of-time-order correlators and entanglement growth, with numerical checks.

existing.note: Section I states this scope in the quoted words.

The solvability is specific: operator correlations vanish except on the light cone and are computed there exactly by quantum channels, the light-cone OTOC is computable, and entanglement growth is exact only for special initial states (products of GHZ states) and light-cone regions. The conclusion says 'much of' the solvability, not all of it. Maximum butterfly velocity is not implied.
existing.value: The authors state that imposing tree-unitarity lifts much of the solvability of dual-unitary circuits to trees: operator correlations vanish except on the light cone, where they can be exactly computed using quantum channels, the light-cone OTOC can be computed with similar techniques, and exact calculations of entanglement growth are possible for a set of special initial conditions.
quotes: Imposing tree-unitarity in turn allowed us to lift much of the solvability of dual-unitary circuits to trees.
in tree-unitary circuits, operator correlations vanish except on the light cone, where they can be exactly computed using quantum channels despite the exponential growth of the number of sites
exact calculations of entanglement growth are possible for a set of special initial conditions
existing.reader_inference: The abstract states the family is 'exactly solvable' without the list of what is solved.

existing.note: The stored value is a fragment of the Introduction. The body says more: a generic tree-unitary circuit has butterfly velocity below 1 along every path (shown by numerical inspection of the channel spectrum, not proved), maximum velocity needs extra maximum-velocity conditions, and a maximum-velocity direction forces correlation functions in other directions to vanish.
existing.value: The authors state that tree-unitarity alone does not give a nontrivial OTOC on the light cone; from numerical inspection of the channel eigenspectrum for a generic tree-unitary circuit they conclude the butterfly velocity is below 1 along any path, that maximum velocity needs additional maximum-velocity conditions, and that a direction of maximum velocity means no other direction can have non-vanishing correlation functions.
quotes: Numerical inspection of the eigenspectrum of the light-cone channels for a 'generic' tree-unitary circuit (from the construction in App. A) shows that indeed no additional such eigenoperators exist.
Thus, we conclude that a generic tree-unitary circuit has butterfly velocity vB < 1 along any given path.
A particular direction being maximum velocity means that no other direction can have non-vanishing correlation functions.
the trade-off between maximal butterfly velocity and non-vanishing correlation functions
existing.reader_inference: The claim for a generic circuit rests on numerical inspection of eigenspectra, so it is not a proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that a brickwork of two-site gates on a tree gives a highly anisotropic light cone, and list that two-point correlations vanish except on the light cone in the direction of the unique fastest path, and that only in that direction do operators spread at the maximum velocity.
quotes: The end result is a highly anisotropic 'light cone' on the tree

(i) two-point correlation functions vanish everywhere except on the light cone in the direction of the unique fastest path; (ii) in the fastest direction, operators spread at the maximum velocity allowed by unitarity;
(iii) in other directions, operators do not spread at the maximum velocity allowed by unitarity;

assertions.value: The paper proves that, for the circuit made of z-site gates applied alternately to the two color classes of a two-color partition of the tree bonds, the number of time steps for an operator to spread from site i to site j is between the graph distance minus one and the graph distance plus one.
assertions.anchor: Section III A, Eq. (1) and its proof
quotes: Specifically, we prove that the number of time steps ti→j for an operator initially localized at site i to spread to site j satisfies the inequality ri,j − 1 ≤ ti→j ≤ ri,j + 1, (1) where ri,j is the graph distance between i and j.
We can then apply z-site unitary gates to all the clusters of a given color in one time step, and then apply them to clusters of the opposite color in the next time step
assertions.certainty_reason: Inequality (1) is stated with its condition (z-site gates on a bond 2-coloring) and proved in Section III A.

assertions.value: The authors define tree-unitarity as the set of conditions that tracing over z minus one pairs of sites gives a term proportional to the identity, which makes the gate an isometry from any pair of opposite legs to the remaining legs.
quotes: These constraints can be extended to more general z, in which we trace over z − 1 pairs of sites and require that we obtain a term proportional to the identity. We denote this set of conditions tree-unitarity.
The conditions from Eq. (6) impose that the unitary gates are isometries from the composite Hilbert spaces corresponding to any pair of opposite legs to the remaining 2(z − 1) legs.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's definition of tree-unitarity, Section III B.

assertions.value: The authors state that tree-unitarity reduces to dual-unitarity for z equal to 2, and that for z above 2 it imposes z independent isometric constraints.
quotes: Dual-unitarity is explicitly recovered for z = 2.
For z > 2 tree-unitarity imposes z independent isometric constraints, whereas for z = 2 the two unitary constraints are equivalent.

assertions.value: The authors report that a numerical estimate for 3-site gates on qubits, from 100 samples, gives a 37-dimensional space of tree-unitary gates, smaller than the 64-dimensional space of all 3-site unitaries on qubits.
quotes: For 3-site gates with q = 2, for each of 100 samples this approach returns that tree-unitary opera- tors form a 37-dimensional space.
This dimension is substantially smaller than that of the space of 3-site unitary operators on qubits, which has dimension 64

assertions.value: The authors describe a numerical algorithm that builds tree-unitary gates by repeated index shuffling and polar decomposition, and state that convergence to a tree-unitary matrix is only observed numerically, not proved.
quotes: If this procedure converges, as numerically seems to be the case for generic initial matrices, it converges to a matrix satisfying all the tree-unitary conditions.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state in Appendix A that convergence is observed numerically only.

assertions.value: The authors show that the kicked Ising model on the tree, built from z-site gates, satisfies tree-unitarity at the dual-unitary parameter values, for any coordination number z, and reduces to a Clifford gate for a special choice of longitudinal field, which allows numerical simulation of large sizes.
quotes: These gates satisfy the treeunitary property [Eq. (6)] for the dual-unitary parameters |J| = |b| = π/4.
This derivation directly extends to the remaining treeunitary conditions and arbitrary z.
Note that U reduces to a Clifford gate if hj = Zπ/8, ∀j; this fact allows for numerical simulations of tree-unitary dynamics for large system sizes.

assertions.value: The authors state that the kicked Ising gates do not exhaust the space of tree-unitary gates and are nongeneric in some aspects, and that perfect tensors form a subset of tree-unitary gates.
quotes: While the resulting gates do not exhaust the full space of tree-unitary gates, and are in some aspects nongeneric
Perfect tensors are thus a subset of tree-unitary gates, with special features discussed in Sec. VI.

assertions.value: The authors state that for z equal to 3 the triunitary gates of an earlier reference can be deformed into 3-site tree-unitary gates, and that tree-unitary gates form a broader class not restricted to z equal to 3.
quotes: For z = 3, the triunitary gates introduced in Ref. 26 can be deformed into 3-site tree-unitary gates (see App. B 3).

assertions.value: The paper shows that for tree-unitary circuits the single-site correlation functions at infinite temperature vanish identically inside the light cone, are generically non-zero on its edge, and vanish outside it by unitarity.
quotes: at infinite temperature, with ⟨•⟩ ≡ tr(•)/tr(1).
For tree-unitary circuits, the single-site correlation functions hence vanish identically inside the light cone, but are generically non-zero on the edge of the light cone.
On the tree, we again have vanishing correlation functions outside the light cone
assertions.certainty_reason: The statement and its condition (infinite temperature, tree-unitary gates) are quoted from Section IV A, where the paper derives it from the isometry conditions.

assertions.value: The authors state that light-cone correlation functions on the tree are obtained by successive application of quantum channels, with the channel sequence set by the path, that there are z(z-1) such channels, and that the expression can be efficiently evaluated for arbitrarily long times.
quotes: For fixed z, there are z(z − 1) choices of such quantum channels.
This expression can be efficiently evaluated for arbitrarily long times.

assertions.value: The authors report, from a heatmap for a generic tree-unitary brickwork circuit, that the correlations are non-zero around a fraction (z-1)/z of the light cone when the first layer acts on one color of bonds and around a fraction 1/z when it acts on the other.
quotes: leading to non-vanishing correlations around a fraction (z − 1)/z of the light cone.
leading to non-vanishing correlations around a fraction 1/z of the light cone.

assertions.value: The authors report that for random tree-unitary gates the light-cone correlation function approaches the equilibrium value of 0 with time scales set by the channel eigenvalues.
quotes: In each case the equilibrium value of 0 is approached, with differing time scales depending on the eigenvalues of the channel M23.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says five random gates and the Figure 6 caption says three random gates.

assertions.value: The authors report that for a generic tree-unitary circuit the light-cone OTOC approaches the trivial value of 1, so the butterfly velocity is below 1, and explain that tree-unitarity does not force the operator front to grow at every step.
quotes: The OTOC approaches the trivial value of 1 on the light cone, indicating that operators do not spread at maximum velocity.
The reason for this difference relative to dual-unitary circuits is that while dual-unitarity requires the operator front to grow with every time step, tree-unitarity does not.

assertions.value: The authors define maximum-velocity conditions on a tree-unitary gate, state that there are z(z-1) of them, that they are stronger than tree-unitarity, and that a gate meeting at least one is a maximum-velocity gate.

When a gate satisfies the maximumvelocity condition for at least one pair of ingoing and outgoing legs, we shall term it a maximum-velocity gate.

assertions.value: The authors report that the kicked Ising model on the tree has a light-cone OTOC that depends on the chosen operators and approaches minus 0.5 or minus 0.25 in the two cases shown, indicating maximum velocity, and that for an operator at the root of a first-layer gate all correlation functions vanish.

assertions.value: The authors state that all correlation functions vanish after one time step if a gate meets at least two maximum-velocity conditions, giving Bernoulli dynamics, which dual-unitary gates cannot realize for q equal to 2 but tree-unitary gates with z above 2 realize in a large class.
quotes: all correlation functions vanish identically after a single time step provided the gate satisfies at least two maximum-velocity conditions.

assertions.value: The paper derives exact entanglement entropy growth of light-cone regions for an initial product of GHZ states on one color of bonds under tree-unitary circuits: the entropy grows exponentially in time and saturates at time equal to the region radius, independent of the specific tree-unitary gates.

assertions.value: The authors define a solvable circuit as one where (a) correlation functions are nonvanishing only on isolated light cones and (b) all light-cone correlations at time t come from a sequence of t quantum channels whose dimensions stay bounded as t grows.
quotes: We consider such a solvable circuit to be one for which (a) correlation functions are constrained to be nonvanishing only on isolated light cones; and (b) all light cone correlations at time t can be obtained by acting with a sequence of t quantum channels whose dimensions remain bounded as t → ∞.

assertions.value: The paper argues that under criterion (a), if the operator weight on the light cone is conserved, a non-maximal butterfly velocity requires the number of sites on the light cone to grow in time; conservation is proved for a class of geometries and otherwise assumed by naturalness.

Thus, if the total operator weight on the light cone is conserved, a non-maximal butterfly velocity requires that the number of sites on the light cone grows in time.
assertions.reader_inference: The general case rests on a fine-tuning (naturalness) argument, not a proof.

assertions.value: The paper derives a lower bound on one minus the light-cone averaged OTOC that is inversely proportional to the number of light-cone sites for fixed light-cone operator weight w, and states that w equals 1 for tree-unitary circuits.

so |Li(a) ∩ Lj(a)| = a + 1, which scales linearly with t = d(i, j); it follows that Dt > O(t) and is therefore unbounded.

papers.what_it_is: A theory paper with numerical examples that derives Lie-Fourier, Taylor and sinc-kernel representations of quantum control landscapes, proves bounds on their spectrum, derivatives and variance, and benchmarks the three representations as surrogate models on a transverse-field Ising system.

The stored value gives the abstract's claims. The body states the bounds: derivatives of any order P are bounded by (omega-max times delta-t) to the P over 2 (Lemma 5), the Lipschitz constant K is at most omega-max times delta-t over 2 in the L1 norm (Lemma 6), and at a critical point a quadratic bound holds with constant at most (omega-max times delta-t) squared over 2. The conditions are bilinear Hamiltonian control with piecewise-constant pulses and a state-fidelity landscape; the appendix proof (Bernstein inequality plus uniform convergence of the Lie-Fourier approximants) covers multiple controls and a generic observable.

assertions.value: The authors derive that a universal 3-qubit DIBoM needs 1121 single-qubit layers and 1120 generalized CZ layers, a total of 13449 parameters, from a decomposition into 28 two-level unitaries.
